title: Scallows Hall Lancaster Memorial

external_narratives.summary: Detailed crew page for 101 Squadron Lancaster III DV270 SR-E piloted by F/O Francis Edward Oliver, aged 21. The aircraft took off on a cross-country training flight and emerged from low cloud, hitting treetops at Binbrook Hall before crashing in Scallows Wood, just missing Scallows Hall.

narrative: On 5 December 1943, Lancaster DV270 of 101 Squadron, based at Ludford Magna, came down at Scallows Hall, Wold Newton, Lincolnshire. Seven crew members were killed, among them the pilot, Flying Officer Francis Edward Oliver, who was 21 years old. Also lost were Flight Officer William Reid, navigator, aged 30; Sergeant Albert Douglas Wells, flight engineer, aged 20; Sergeant John Winton Anderson, bomb aimer, aged 30; Sergeant Stanley George Burton, wireless operator, aged 20; and Sergeant Robert Stanley Bradbury, air gunner, aged 20. The fates of the remaining crew members aboard that night are not fully recorded.
community_connection: On the 16th July 1978, a memorial to 101 Squadron was unveiled at Ludford Magna by AVM Robert 'Bob' Blucke DSO AFC. This event was funded by funds raised from veterans and over 300 people attended. This memorial marks the genesis of the 101 Squadron Association.

memorial_details:
On the wall of the White Hart pub is a bronze plaque dedicated in 2007 to the 740 101 Sqn aircrew and ground crew who were killed while serving at Ludford Magna between June 1943 and May 1945.

101 Squadron centenary memorial On Saturday 23rd September 2017 over 140 members of the 101 Squadron Association gathered at the National Memorial Arboretum, Alrewas, Staffordshire to witness the unveiling and dedication of a new memorial to celebrate 100 years of service by 101 Squadron RAF.

Memorial Unveiling and Remembrance Service (16th July 1978): A memorial to 101 Squadron was unveiled at Ludford Magna by AVM Robert ‘Bob’ Blucke DSO AFC. Over 300 attendees followed the unveiling with a tea provided by the Ludford WI.
